MODERN FABER _

* * *

TO THE FABERS:

Faber is an old word for a maker — the smith at the forge, the carpenter at the bench. Homo faber: the one who makes. There have never been fewer — not for lack of wanting, but because talking about making became easier than making. The feed rewards the announcement, not the object, and whole rooms fill with people circling the work they say they want to do.

Modern Faber is a room for the ones who still make. One rule holds it together: come back every week with something real, and say what you changed. No audience, no applause — only other fabers paying attention to the details you almost skipped. That attention costs something. It is meant to. Keep the rhythm long enough and you are left with a body of work, a sharper eye, and the few people you actually want beside you at the bench.

* * *

HOW WE OPERATE:

REFERRAL. No applications. A faber has to know your work well enough to put your name up, and the vote has to be unanimous — one no keeps the door shut. What earns a nod is an artifact with taste, not a title or a plan. AI-made is fine; raw Claude or Codex is obvious — what you decide on top of it is not.

COMMUNITY. An open agora — bring up what you are stuck on, show work still rough in the middle. You hold your seat with what you share and what you answer.

MEETUPS. Three or four to a table, never more, matched at random. Ninety minutes dense enough that you leave holding something you could not have reached alone — and wanting the next one.
